after.name: Question 1
after.problem: Calculate the area of the parallelogram spanned by $\text{u}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 4\end{aligned}]$ and $\text{v}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{4} \\ -\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
First, we construct a matrix where the columns are made up of the components of the corresponding vectors:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}-2 & \frac{1}{4} \\ 4 & -\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}]
$$

Then, we find the determinant:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(M) & =|\begin{aligned}-2 & \frac{1}{4} \\ 4 & -\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-2)\cdot (-\frac{1}{2})-\frac{1}{4}\cdot 4 \\  & =1-1 \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

The absolute value of $det(M)$ gives the area $A$ of the parallelogram:

$$
A=|\,0\,|=0
$$

after.worked_solution:
First, we construct a matrix where the columns are made up of the components of the corresponding vectors:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}-\sqrt{7} & a \\ 5 & -10\end{aligned}]
$$

Then, we find the determinant:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(M) & =|\begin{aligned}-\sqrt{7} & a \\ 5 & -10\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-\sqrt{7})(-10)-a\cdot 5 \\  & =10\sqrt{7}-5a\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, setting the expression for the determinant equal to $0$ and solving for $a,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}10\sqrt{7}-5a & =0 \\ 5a & =10\sqrt{7} \\ a & =2\sqrt{7}.\end{aligned}
$$
